prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Time for common sense: trust people, not government. The Conservatives set out to free families, entrepreneurs, schools, hospitals and police from meddling and bureaucracy; to respect the institutions bigger than any one of us; and to restore national self-government.

- Family and schools: Back marriage and parenting with lower taxes (extra Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; new Married Couple’s Allowance via transferable allowances). Create Free Schools run by heads and governors; cut red tape; restore discipline; let successful schools expand; allow new faith/parent/charitable schools; Parent’s Guarantee to trigger Ofsted and change failing management; Progress Centres for disruptive pupils. No top‑up fees; student loan repayments only above £20,000. Endow universities for independence.

- Law and order: More police, less paperwork; “cops in shops” and parish constables. Tenfold increase in Secure Training Centre places; mandatory jail for dealers selling to under‑16s; tougher action near schools. Honest sentencing (end automatic early release); work in prison, reparations to victims; lifelong supervision options for sex offenders; protect children online. Put victims first with named contacts and transparency; reform self-defence and double jeopardy law.

- Economy: A tax‑cutting, deregulatory government. Fund £8bn of targeted tax cuts by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence: abolish taxes on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; cut fuel duty by at least 6p; abolish IR35; simplify CGT. Transparent public accounts and regulatory budgets via new Commissions; cut the cost of regulation yearly. Keep the pound; no early euro; strengthen Bank of England independence and fiscal discipline.

- NHS and patients: Match funding plans but end political interference. Patient’s Guarantee of maximum waits set by clinical need, with choice of NHS or private provision paid by the NHS. Restore ward sisters’ authority; bring back matrons; expand specialist surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund to end the postcode lottery. End tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable; increase hospice funding.

- Older people: Respect and independence, not means-testing. Raise the basic state pension (extra for over‑75s); option to consolidate winter fuel/TV licence into higher, tax‑free pension. Remove a million from tax via higher age allowance; abolish compulsory annuitisation at 75; develop funded pension options for the young; protect savers facing long‑term care.

- Nationhood and security: In Europe, not run by Europe. Keep the pound and the veto; renegotiate Nice; reserve powers in UK law; veto further transfers without a referendum. No EU army outside NATO; back our armed forces, end political correctness, reach full manning, exempt forces from the ECHR like others; support US missile defence; maintain independent deterrent. Aim for global free trade by 2020; reform EU aid; double charity‑channelled aid; focus on governance. Asylum: secure reception centres until decisions; safe‑country rule; new Removals Agency.

- Society and welfare: Champion civil society with an Office of Civil Society; scrap charities’ irrecoverable VAT using euro‑prep funds. Replace New Deal with Britain Works—pay by sustained jobs; Can Work, Must Work. Support lone parents into work; fairer rules for disabled savers; rehab‑focused incapacity agency; national anti‑fraud squad and clean NI records.

- Town and country: Foot and Mouth Recovery Strategy; reform CAP/CFP; honesty in labelling; cut rural business rates; save post offices with a benefit card; abolish top‑down housing targets; protect “Blue Belts”. Regenerate cities via local Regeneration Companies, brownfield first, stronger right‑to‑buy and rent‑to‑mortgage; tackle “neighbours from hell”. Transport: invest for all users; 80mph where safe; Brit Disc for foreign lorries; revive rail; cut fuel duty 6p; cut taxes on cleaner fuels. Climate action through trading, efficiency, innovation—not blunt levies.

- Culture and media: Free the arts from state dependence with a £3bn endowment (privatise Channel 4, keep its remit); boost tourism; protect school sport and playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; single light‑touch comms regulator; fair BBC oversight; open access for religious broadcasters.

- Democracy: Power down to effective local councils (“free councils”); local referendums on big Council Tax rises; scrap regional quangos and assemblies; English Votes for English Laws; strengthen Lords’ independence with an elected element; tougher Commons scrutiny; fewer ministers, MPs and spin doctors; keep first‑past‑the‑post. Steadfast for the Union and the Belfast Agreement—with decommissioning and firm security.

Time to deliver. Time for common sense.
